# temps_notification_provider (Resource)

A webhook notification provider. Temps posts alerts (failed deployments, backups, monitors) to its URL. The server never returns the URL or header values, so Terraform keeps them from configuration; after an import, set them in configuration again. Required API key permissions: `notification_providers:read`, `notification_providers:create`, `notification_providers:write`, `notification_providers:delete`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_notification_provider" "alerts" {
  name         = "Team alerts"
  url          = "https://hooks.example.com/alerts"
  method       = "POST"
  timeout_secs = 10
  headers = {
    Authorization = "Bearer ${var.alerts_token}"
  }
}

variable "alerts_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.
- `url` (String, Sensitive) http(s) URL notifications are sent to. Stored as a secret.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether notifications are sent. Defaults to `true`.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Extra request headers. Their values are stored as secrets.
- `method` (String) HTTP method: `POST` (default), `PUT` or `PATCH`.
- `timeout_secs` (Number) Request timeout in seconds, 1 to 120. Defaults to 30.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Provider ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <provider_id>. Temps never returns the URL or header values, so set them in
# configuration again after importing.
terraform import temps_notification_provider.alerts 4
```
